questions.question: The RBI launched the Lead Bank Scheme (LBS) to mobilise deposits and step-up lending to weaker sections of the economy. When was the scheme launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1969**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) launched the **Lead Bank Scheme (LBS)** in **1969**.
 
• The primary aim of the Lead Bank Scheme was to mobilize deposits and **enhance lending** to **weaker sections of society.**
 
• The scheme was part of a broader initiative to promote **financial inclusion** and ensure that banking services reach underbanked and unbanked areas.
 
• Under this scheme, a designated bank, known as the Lead Bank, is responsible for the overall development and banking coverage of its assigned district.
 
• The scheme fosters **coordination and collaboration** among various banks and financial institutions to achieve inclusive growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Financial Inclusion:**

 
 
• It refers to the process of ensuring access to financial services and timely and adequate credit for all, especially vulnerable groups such as weaker sections and low-income groups, at an affordable cost.
 
• Financial inclusion aims to eliminate barriers and provide financial tools to all individuals and businesses to effectively manage their finances.
 
 
 
• **Priority Sector Lending (PSL):**
 
 
• Under PSL, banks are required to allocate a portion of their lending to specified sectors like agriculture, micro and small enterprises, and others that have a significant impact on large sections of the population.
 
• PSL is a major component of the Lead Bank Scheme aimed at directing more credit to priority sectors.
 
 
 
• **District Credit Plans (DCPs):**
 
 
• These are formulated under the Lead Bank Scheme to ensure a coordinated approach to credit planning.
 
• DCPs involve the preparation of a plan for each district, identifying the credit potential and setting targets for lending by banks operating in the district.
 
 
 
• **Service Area Approach (SAA):**
 
 
• Introduced in 1989, SAA is a part of the Lead Bank Scheme where each bank branch is assigned specific villages for providing financial services.
 
• This approach ensures that all villages are covered by banking services and helps in better monitoring and performance of rural branches.

questions.question: Which detergents are also used in toothpaste?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anionic detergents**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Anionic detergents are commonly used in **toothpaste due to their effective cleansing properties.**
 
• **Sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS)** is a prevalent anionic detergent found in many toothpaste formulations.
 
• Anionic detergents help in creating foam, which aids in the mechanical removal of food particles and plaque.
 
• These detergents are also responsible for the dispersion of ingredients in toothpaste, ensuring a uniform mixture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Surfactants:**

 
 
• Surfactants are compounds that lower the surface tension between two substances, such as a solid and a liquid.
 
• They are a key ingredient in many cleaning products, including toothpaste, detergents, and shampoos.
 
• Anionic surfactants, like sodium lauryl sulfate, are particularly effective in removing dirt and oil.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (SLS):**
 
 
• SLS is one of the most commonly used surfactants in toothpaste and other personal care products.
 
• It is known for its ability to produce a rich lather, which helps in the thorough cleaning of teeth.
 
• Despite its effectiveness, SLS can cause irritation in some individuals, leading to the development of alternative formulations.
 
 
 
• **Toothpaste Ingredients:**
 
 
• Common ingredients in toothpaste include abrasives, fluoride, flavoring agents, and humectants.
 
• Abrasives help in removing plaque and stains from the teeth, while fluoride strengthens tooth enamel.
 
• Humectants prevent the toothpaste from drying out, ensuring it remains usable over time.
 
 
 
• **Non-Ionic Detergents:**
 
 
• Non-ionic detergents are another class of surfactants that do not carry any charge.
 
• They are less likely to cause irritation and are often used in products designed for sensitive skin.
 
• While effective in cleaning, they are not as commonly used in toothpaste as anionic detergents.

questions.question: Which of the following states of India does the Konkan Railway connect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra and Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Konkan Railway connects the states of **Maharashtra and Karnataka** in India.
 
• It runs along the western coast of India, providing a critical link between Mumbai (Maharashtra) and Mangalore (Karnataka).
 
• The railway line covers a distance of approximately **741 kilometres**.
 
• It was officially inaugurated on **January 26, 1998**, by the then Prime Minister of India, Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
 
• The Konkan Railway is known for its engineering marvels, including numerous **tunnels and bridges** that traverse the challenging terrain of the Western Ghats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Western Ghats**

 
 
• The Western Ghats is a mountain range that runs parallel to the western coast of India.
 
• It is recognized as one of the world's eight** "hottest hotspots"** of biological diversity.
 
• The Konkan Railway passes through this region, making the journey scenic and challenging for engineers.
 
 
 
• **Engineering Feats**
 
 
• The Konkan Railway includes several long tunnels and tall bridges.
 
• Some of the notable tunnels include the **Karbude Tunnel (6.5 km) and the Natuwadi Tunnel (4.3 km).**
 
• The Panvalnadi Bridge is one of the highest viaducts in Asia.
 
 
 
• **Tourism Impact**
 
 
• The Konkan Railway has boosted tourism in the coastal regions of Maharashtra, Goa, and Karnataka.
 
• It provides easy access to several tourist destinations like Goa, Ratnagiri, and Mangalore.
 
• The scenic route attracts numerous travellers, especially during the monsoon season.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance**
 
 
• The railway line has significantly improved the connectivity and economic development of the Konkan region.
 
• It facilitates the transportation of goods, including agricultural produce and seafood, from the coastal areas to major markets.
 
• It has also enhanced the mobility of people, contributing to the growth of trade and commerce.

questions.question: Kautilya has mentioned the concept of Saptanga Rajya to understand the State with seven organs and one of them is Danda, which means:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kautilya, also known as Chanakya, in his treatise** "Arthashastra" **mentions the Saptanga theory to describe the seven essential elements of a state.
 
• **Danda**, one of the seven elements, signifies the armed forces or the military force of the state.
 
• According to Kautilya, the state's power and authority are maintained through Danda, ensuring law and order.
 
• The concept underlines the importance of military might for the protection and enforcement of the state's policies.
 
• The seven elements in the Saptanga theory are: **Swami (the ruler), Amatya (the ministers), Janapada (the territory and the people), Durga (the fort), Kosha (the treasury), Danda (the force), and Mitra (the ally).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saptanga Theory**

 
 
• The Saptanga theory is an ancient Indian model of statecraft articulated by Kautilya in the Arthashastra.
 
• It outlines seven crucial elements that constitute a well-functioning state.
 
• Each of these elements must function effectively for the prosperity and stability of the state.
 
 
 
• **Kautilya (Chanakya)**
 
 
• Kautilya, also known as Chanakya or Vishnugupta, was an ancient Indian teacher, philosopher, economist, jurist, and royal advisor.
 
• He authored the ancient Indian political treatise called the "Arthashastra".
 
• Kautilya played a key role in the establishment of the Maurya Empire.
 
 
 
• **Arthashastra**
 
 
• The Arthashastra is an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy.
 
• It was written in Sanskrit and is attributed to Kautilya (Chanakya).
 
• The text covers various topics including governance, administration, law, economics, and military strategy.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of Danda**
 
 
• Danda, or force, is crucial for maintaining internal order and external defense.
 
• It emphasizes the role of the military in protecting the state and enforcing its laws.
 
• A strong and disciplined military is considered essential for the state's survival and prosperity.

questions.question: The Companies Act, __________ is an Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to companies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2013**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Companies Act, 2013** is an Act of the Parliament of India which regulates the incorporation, responsibilities, and dissolution of companies.
 
• It replaced the Companies Act, 1956, bringing significant changes to the legal framework governing Indian companies.
 
• The Act was enacted on 29 August 2013 and came into force on 1 April 2014.
 
• It introduced new concepts such as one-person companies, corporate social responsibility (CSR), and enhanced disclosure norms.
 
• The Act aims to improve corporate governance and protect investor interests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)**

 
 
• The Companies Act, 2013 mandates certain companies to spend a minimum amount on CSR activities.
 
• Companies with a net worth of Rs. 500 crores or more, or turnover of Rs. 1000 crores or more, or net profit of Rs. 5 crores or more during any financial year are required to spend at least 2% of their average net profits on CSR.
 
• This provision aims to ensure that companies contribute to societal welfare and development.
 
 
 
• **One-Person Company (OPC)**
 
 
• The concept of OPC allows a single individual to form a company, thereby providing a new avenue for solo entrepreneurs.
 
• OPCs have simplified compliance requirements compared to private limited companies.
 
• This has been introduced to encourage individual entrepreneurship and formalize small businesses.
 
 
 
• **National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT)**
 
 
• The Companies Act, 2013 established the NCLT to adjudicate issues related to companies in India.
 
• The NCLT consolidates the corporate jurisdiction of various authorities such as the Company Law Board, Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction, and the Appellate Authority for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction.
 
• The NCLT provides a single window for corporate dispute resolution.
 
 
 
• **Enhanced Disclosure Norms**
 
 
• The Act mandates increased transparency through enhanced disclosure requirements in financial statements and board reports.
 
• Companies are required to disclose their policies on CSR, risk management, and other significant matters.
 
• This aims to promote better governance and accountability.

questions.question: Identify the atomic number of an element that belongs to group 17.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**53**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The atomic number 53 corresponds to the element **Iodine (I).**
 
• Iodine is a member of Group 17 in the periodic table, known as the halogens.
 
• Group 17 elements are known for their high reactivity and include** Fluorine, Chlorine, Bromine, Iodine, and Astatine.**
 
• Iodine is essential for the production of thyroid hormones in the human body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Halogens**

 
 
• Group 17 elements are called halogens, derived from Greek words meaning "salt-former".
 
• They are highly reactive nonmetals and can form salts when they react with metals.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Table**
 
 
• The periodic table arranges elements in order of increasing atomic number.
 
• Groups (vertical columns) in the periodic table share similar chemical properties.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Number**
 
 
• The atomic number of an element is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• It defines the identity of an element and its position in the periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Iodine Uses**
 
 
• Iodine is used in medical antiseptics, dyes, and photographic chemicals.
 
• It is also a crucial nutrient for thyroid function, preventing goiter and other health issues.

questions.question: How much maximum amount of loan can be taken from Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (2015)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 lakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) was launched by the Government of India in April 2015.
 
• The primary objective of PMMY is to provide financial support to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.
 
• The maximum loan amount that can be availed under PMMY is up to Rs. 10 lakh.
 
• Loans under PMMY are categorized into three products: Shishu (up to Rs. 50,000), Kishore (Rs. 50,001 to Rs. 5 lakh), and Tarun (Rs. 5,01,000 to Rs. 10 lakh).
 
• PMMY aims to promote entrepreneurship among the youth and encourage small businesses to grow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**

 
 
• Any Indian citizen with a business plan for a non-farm income-generating activity can avail of a loan under PMMY.
 
• The applicant must be at least 18 years old.
 
• Individuals, proprietary concerns, partnership firms, and other legal entities are eligible for the loan.
 
 
 
• **Types of Loans:**
 
 
• **Shishu:** Covering loans up to Rs. 50,000, aimed at startups and early-stage businesses.
 
• **Kishore:** Covering loans ranging from Rs. 50,001 to Rs. 5 lakh, for businesses in the growth phase.
 
• **Tarun:** Covering loans from Rs. 5,01,000 to Rs. 10 lakh, for established businesses looking to scale up.
 
 
 
• **Interest Rates:**
 
 
• Interest rates under PMMY are decided by the lending institution, based on the RBI guidelines.
 
• Generally, these loans are offered at competitive rates to make them affordable for small entrepreneurs.
 
 
 
• **Application Process:**
 
 
• Interested applicants can approach any of the lending institutions, including public sector banks, private sector banks, regional rural banks, and microfinance institutions.
 
• The application process involves submitting a detailed business plan and relevant documents as required by the lending institution.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• Since its inception, PMMY has significantly contributed to the financial inclusion of small and micro-enterprises in India.
 
• It has helped in the creation of millions of jobs and has empowered women entrepreneurs.

questions.question: Chandragupta Maurya overthrew which of the following dynasties of ancient India to establish the Mauryan empire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nanda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya** established the Mauryan Empire by overthrowing the Nanda Dynasty in the late 4th century BCE.
 
• The Nanda Dynasty was known for its wealth and powerful military and was the ruling dynasty in the region of Magadha before the Mauryan Empire.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya was supported by his mentor and advisor, **Chanakya (Kautilya)**, in his efforts to overthrow the Nandas.
 
• The final ruler of the Nanda Dynasty, Dhana Nanda, was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya, leading to the establishment of the Mauryan rule.
 
• The Mauryan Empire, under Chandragupta Maurya, marked the beginning of a significant period in Indian history, characterized by political unity and the spread of Buddhism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nanda Dynasty**

 
 
• The Nanda Dynasty was founded by Mahapadma Nanda, who is often considered the first historical emperor of India.
 
• The Nandas are known for their centralized administration and large army, which included a significant number of war elephants.
 
• The dynasty ruled from approximately 345 to 322 BCE and was known for its immense wealth and extensive control over the Ganges plain.
 
 
 
• **Chanakya (Kautilya)**
 
 
• Chanakya was an ancient Indian teacher, philosopher, economist, jurist, and royal advisor.
 
• He is traditionally identified as the author of the Arthashastra, an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy.
 
• Chanakya played a crucial role in the establishment of the Mauryan Empire and was the chief advisor to Chandragupta Maurya.
 
 
 
• **Mauryan Empire**
 
 
• The Mauryan Empire, founded by Chandragupta Maurya, lasted from 322 to 185 BCE and was one of the largest empires in Indian history.
 
• Under the rule of Ashoka, the empire saw the widespread adoption of Buddhism and the spread of Buddhist principles throughout Asia.
 
• The Mauryan administration was highly organized and included a vast network of spies and a standing army.
 
 
 
• **Magadha**
 
 
• Magadha was an ancient Indian kingdom located in the eastern part of India, in what is now Bihar.
 
• It played a central role in the rise of several significant Indian empires, including the Maurya and Gupta Empires.
 
• The region was known for its strategic location, fertile land, and rich mineral resources, which contributed to its power and influence.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about Bibi ka Maqbara at Aurangabad?

options.text: It is an imitation of the Taj Mahal due to its similar designs.
It was built by Mughal prince Azam Shah.
It is built completely with marble.
It is the burial place of Aurangzeb's wife, Rabia-ud-Durrani.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is built completely with marble.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bibi ka Maqbara** is not entirely built with marble; only the dome and some parts are constructed with marble.
 
• The rest of the structure is made of basalt and lime plaster, giving it a distinct architectural style.
 
• It was built by **Mughal prince Azam Shah** in memory of his mother, Dilras Banu Begum, also known as Rabia-ud-Durrani.
 
• Bibi ka Maqbara is often referred to as the "Taj of the Deccan" due to its similar design to the Taj Mahal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bibi ka Maqbara**

 
 
• It is located in Aurangabad, Maharashtra, India.
 
• The monument was commissioned by Aurangzeb's son, Azam Shah, in 1660.
 
• The architectural design was done by Ata-ullah, who was the son of Ustad Ahmad Lahauri, the principal designer of the Taj Mahal.
 
• The mausoleum's layout and surrounding gardens follow the traditional Mughal Charbagh (four-quartered) garden layout.
 
 
 
• **Taj Mahal**
 
 
• It is located in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• It was commissioned by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• The construction began in 1632 and was completed in 1653.
 
• The Taj Mahal is entirely built of white marble and is considered one of the finest examples of Mughal architecture.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Architecture**
 
 
• Mughal architecture is a unique blend of Islamic, Persian, Turkish, and Indian architectural styles.
 
• It flourished between the 16th and 18th centuries under the Mughal Empire.
 
• Key features include large bulbous domes, slender minarets, large halls, massive vaulted gateways, and delicate ornamentation.
 
• Famous examples include the Red Fort, Jama Masjid, and Fatehpur Sikri.
 
 
 
• **Basalt**
 
 
• Basalt is a common extrusive igneous rock formed from the rapid cooling of basaltic lava.
 
• It is primarily composed of plagioclase, pyroxene, and olivine minerals.
 
• Basalt is known for its durability and is often used in construction.

questions.question: Who among the following is a Hindustani classical vocalist?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kishori Amonkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kishori Amonkar was a renowned Hindustani classical vocalist known for her contributions to Indian classical music.
 
• She was a leading exponent of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana.
 
• Her music was characterized by its emotional depth and technical precision.
 
• She received numerous accolades, including the Padma Bhushan in 1987 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2002.
 
• Amonkar was also known for her innovative approach and experimentation within the framework of classical music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustani Classical Music**

 
 
• It is one of the two major traditions of Indian classical music, the other being Carnatic music.
 
• This tradition dates back to the Vedic times, around 1000 BCE.
 
• It is typically performed in two main genres: Dhrupad and Khayal.
 
• Ragas and Talas form the basic framework for improvisation and composition.
 
 
 
• **Gharanas**
 
 
• A gharana is a system of social organization linking musicians or dancers by lineage or apprenticeship, and by adherence to a particular musical style.
 
• Some well-known gharanas in Hindustani classical music include Jaipur-Atrauli, Gwalior, Kirana, and Patiala.
 
• Each gharana has its own unique style and repertoire.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards**
 
 
• These are one of the highest civilian awards in India, given in various disciplines/fields of activities such as art, social work, public affairs, etc.
 
• They are classified into three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri.
 
 
 
• **Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana**
 
 
• It was founded by Alladiya Khan in the late 19th century.
 
• This gharana is known for its complex and intricate raga structures.
 
• Prominent exponents include Kesarbai Kerkar, Mogubai Kurdikar, and Kishori Amonkar.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles prohibits employment of children under 14 years of age in factories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 24**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 24** of the Indian Constitution prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, or any other hazardous employment.
 
• This provision ensures that children are protected from exploitation and harmful work conditions.
 
• Article 24 is part of the Fundamental Rights enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The article aims to safeguard the health and development of children by preventing their engagement in hazardous occupations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986**

 
 
• This Act prohibits the employment of children in certain specified hazardous occupations and processes.
 
• It regulates the conditions of work for children in non-hazardous occupations.
 
 
 
• **Article 21A**
 
 
• Article 21A of the Indian Constitution mandates the state to provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• This provision complements Article 24 by ensuring that children are in school rather than at work.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education Act, 2009**
 
 
• This Act operationalizes Article 21A and ensures every child's right to education.
 
• It mandates that private schools reserve 25% of their seats for children from economically weaker sections.
 
 
 
• **Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015**
 
 
• This Act provides for the care, protection, and rehabilitation of children in conflict with the law and those in need of care and protection.
 
• It includes provisions for the protection of children from exploitation and abuse.

questions.question: Nahid Siddiqui is a famous classical dancer in _______ genre.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Nahid Siddiqui is a renowned classical dancer specializing in the **Kathak** genre.
 
• She has significantly contributed to the promotion and revival of Kathak dance both in India and internationally.
 
• Nahid Siddiqui is acclaimed for her innovative choreography and mastery over the intricate techniques of Kathak.
 
• She has received multiple awards and recognitions for her outstanding contributions to the field of classical dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak Dance**

 
 
• Originated in northern India and is one of the eight classical dance forms in India.
 
• Known for its intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures.
 
• Historically, Kathak dancers traveled and performed across the subcontinent, evolving the dance form into a storytelling medium.
 
• Kathak has influences from Mughal culture and incorporates both Hindu and Persian elements.
 
 
 
• **Gharanas in Kathak**
 
 
• There are three primary gharanas (schools) of Kathak: Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras.
 
• Each gharana has its unique style, emphasis on techniques, and traditional compositions.
 
 
 
• **Prominent Kathak Dancers**
 
 
• Birju Maharaj: A leading exponent of the Lucknow gharana.
 
• Shovana Narayan: Known for her innovative approach and contributions to the modern Kathak.
 
• Kumudini Lakhia: A celebrated Kathak dancer and choreographer.
 
 
 
• **Costumes in Kathak**
 
 
• Female dancers usually wear anarkali suits, lehengas, and dupattas.
 
• Male dancers typically wear dhotis or churidars with kurtas and angarakhas.
 
• Jewelry and ghungroos (ankle bells) are integral to the costume, enhancing the visual and auditory experience.

questions.question: If the MPC = 0.8, what is the likely value of the Government expenditure multiplier for a standard national output (aggregate demand) function Y = C + I + G?

__
 
• The government expenditure multiplier is calculated as 1 / (1 - MPC).
 
• With an MPC (Marginal Propensity to Consume) of 0.8, the multiplier formula becomes 1 / (1 - 0.8).
 
• This simplifies to 1 / 0.2.
 
• Therefore, the government expenditure multiplier is 5.

• **Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC)**

 
 
• It is the fraction of additional income that a household consumes rather than saves.
 
• An MPC of 0.8 means that for every additional dollar received, 80 cents are spent.
 
 
 
• **Multiplier Effect**
 
 
• The multiplier effect refers to the proportional amount of increase in final income that results from an injection of spending.
 
• The size of the multiplier depends on the MPC; the higher the MPC, the larger the multiplier.
 
 
 
• **Aggregate Demand**
 
 
• It is the total demand for final goods and services in an economy at a given time.
 
• Aggregate demand includes consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports.
 
 
 
• **Government Spending**

questions.question: Identify the correct statement related to metallic character.

options.text: Metallic character stays the same across a period and decreases the same down a group.
Metallic character decreases across a group and stays the same down a group.
Metallic character decreases across a period and increases down a group.
Metallic character increases across a period and decreases down a group.

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Metallic character** refers to the level of reactivity of a metal.
 
• Across a period from left to right, **metallic character decreases** because elements become less willing to lose electrons.
 
• Down a group, the **metallic character increases** due to the increase in atomic size, which makes it easier for atoms to lose electrons.
 
• Elements on the left side of the periodic table (alkali metals) have the highest metallic character, whereas elements on the right side (noble gases) have the least.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ionization Energy:** The energy required to remove an electron from an atom. It increases across a period and decreases down a group.
 
• **Electronegativity:** The ability of an atom to attract electrons. It increases across a period and decreases down a group.
 
• **Atomic Radius:** The size of an atom. It decreases across a period and increases down a group.
 
• **Non-metallic Character:** Opposite of metallic character, it increases across a period and decreases down a group.
 
• **Periodic Trends:** Understanding these trends helps in predicting the chemical behavior of elements.

• The mitochondria are known as the **powerhouses of the cell** because they are the primary site of ATP (adenosine triphosphate) production.
 
• ATP is the main energy currency of the cell, and it is produced during the process of **oxidative phosphorylation** within the mitochondria.
 
• The inner membrane of the mitochondria contains structures called **cristae**, which increase the surface area for ATP production.
 
• Mitochondria have their own DNA and ribosomes, allowing them to produce some of their own proteins necessary for energy production.

• **Oxidative Phosphorylation**

 
 
• This is the process by which ATP is formed as electrons are transferred from electron donors to electron acceptors such as oxygen, in the electron transport chain.
 
• It takes place in the inner mitochondrial membrane and involves a series of protein complexes known as the **electron transport chain**.
 
• The energy released from these reactions is used to pump protons across the mitochondrial membrane, creating a proton gradient.
 
• The return flow of protons through ATP synthase drives the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondrial DNA**
 
 
• Mitochondria contain their own genome, which is separate from the nuclear DNA of the cell.
 
• This mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is inherited maternally and encodes essential components required for mitochondrial function.
 
• Mutations in mtDNA can lead to a range of mitochondrial diseases, often affecting organs and tissues with high energy demands.
 
 
 
• **Energy Metabolism**
 
 
• Mitochondria play a crucial role in energy metabolism through the citric acid cycle (Krebs cycle) and the electron transport chain.
 
• The citric acid cycle generates high-energy electron carriers (NADH and FADH2) that feed into the electron transport chain.
 
• These metabolic pathways are essential for converting nutrients into usable energy in the form of ATP.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondrial Dysfunction**
 
 
• Mitochondrial dysfunction can lead to a range of diseases, including neurodegenerative disorders, cardiovascular diseases, and metabolic syndromes.
 
• It is often characterized by reduced ATP production, increased production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), and impaired cellular function.
 
• Research into mitochondrial medicine is ongoing, aiming to develop therapies for conditions linked to mitochondrial dysfunction.

• A widely used food preservative that inhibits the growth of mold, yeast, and some bacteria.
 
• Commonly used in acidic foods like salad dressings, carbonated drinks, and fruit juices.
 
 
 
• **Table Salt (Sodium Chloride):**

questions.question: Under which article is the Finance Commission constituted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 280**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Finance Commission of India is constituted under **Article 280** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The President of India appoints the Finance Commission every **five years** or at such earlier time as he considers necessary.
 
• The main function of the Finance Commission is to **recommend the distribution of taxes between the Union and the States**.
 
• The Finance Commission also determines the principles that govern the grants-in-aid to the states from the Consolidated Fund of India.
 
• The Commission consists of a Chairman and **four other members** appointed by the President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 280**

 
 
• It provides for the establishment of a Finance Commission to define the financial relations between the central government and the state governments.
 
• The Commission is required to make recommendations on matters such as the **distribution of net proceeds of taxes** between the Centre and the States, and the allocation among the States of the respective shares of such proceeds.
 
• It also looks into the measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of the Panchayats and Municipalities in the state based on the recommendations made by the Finance Commission of the State.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Bodies**
 
 
• Constitutional bodies are those that are established by the Constitution of India.
 
• Examples include the Election Commission, Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), and the Finance Commission.
 
• These bodies derive their power and authority directly from the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Grants-in-aid**
 
 
• These are funds provided by the central government to state governments.
 
• The purpose of these grants is to assist states in meeting expenditure on specific projects or schemes.
 
• They play a crucial role in ensuring that states have adequate resources to implement policies and programs.
 
 
 
• **Tax Devolution**
 
 
• Tax devolution refers to the distribution of the revenue collected through central taxes to the states.
 
• This ensures a balanced distribution of financial resources between the Centre and the States.
 
• The Finance Commission recommends the formula for this distribution.

questions.question: How is the image formed by a plane mirror?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Virtual and erect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A plane mirror forms an image that is **virtual**, meaning the image cannot be projected onto a screen.
 
• The image formed is **erect**, maintaining the same orientation as the object.
 
• Images formed by plane mirrors are also **laterally inverted**, meaning the left and right sides are swapped.
 
• The distance of the image from the mirror is equal to the distance of the object from the mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Virtual Image**

 
 
• A virtual image is formed when rays of light appear to diverge from a point behind the mirror.
 
• It cannot be captured on a screen as it does not involve actual light convergence.
 
 
 
• **Lateral Inversion**
 
 
• Lateral inversion refers to the reversal of the left and right sides in the image formed by a mirror.
 
• This is why text appears reversed when viewed in a mirror.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Plane Mirrors**
 
 
• Plane mirrors have a flat reflective surface.
 
• They produce images with the same size as the object.
 
• The image is always at the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front of it.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Plane Mirrors**
 
 
• Used in everyday items such as bathroom mirrors and dressing mirrors.
 
• Important in optical instruments like periscopes and kaleidoscopes.
 
• Used in rear-view mirrors in vehicles to provide a virtual image of the road behind.

questions.question: The Self-Respect movement was led by whom among the following social reformers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**EV Ramaswamy Naicker**__.

__Key Points__

__
 
• **EV Ramaswamy Naicker**, popularly known as Periyar, was the leader of the Self-Respect Movement.
 
• The movement was initiated in the **1920s in Tamil Nadu** to promote self-respect among the backward classes.
 
• Periyar aimed to eradicate the caste system and promote rationalism, self-respect, and social equality.
 
• The movement was crucial in the socio-political landscape of Tamil Nadu, influencing **Dravidian politics**.
 
• It emphasized **education, women's rights, and the abolition of untouchability**.

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Periyar's Early Life:**

 
 
• Born on September 17, 1879, in Erode, Tamil Nadu.
 
• Initially involved in the Indian National Congress, he left due to its caste-based discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Key Principles of the Self-Respect Movement:**
 
 
• Advocated for rational thinking and self-respect.
 
• Opposed Brahminical dominance and the caste hierarchy.
 
• Encouraged the use of the Tamil language and culture.
 
 
 
• **Women's Rights:**
 
 
• Periyar promoted women's rights, including property rights and the right to education.
 
• Opposed child marriage and promoted widow remarriage.
 
 
 
• **Dravidar Kazhagam:**
 
 
• Periyar founded the Dravidar Kazhagam (DK) in 1944 to continue his social reform agenda.
 
• DK played a significant role in the rise of Dravidian political parties like DMK and AIADMK.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Periyar's ideas continue to influence contemporary social and political movements in Tamil Nadu.
 
• His birthday is celebrated as ""Social Justice Day"" in the state.
